grok.response:
**Do not treat 60.0476% as a forecast.** It is only 1.10 × 54.5887%. Nothing below is TEST-tuned. Old TEST numbers are development-exposed and must not choose hyperparameters, fusion weights, or a winner.

## Recommendation

The baseline is already a strong shape descriptor plus a local density head. Hydra / MultiRocket / hybrids and LOF in the same space all losing, and 24D/42D routers losing, is evidence against three tempting moves: more Rocket channels, a different density formula on the same 4096-D Euclidean graph, and **dropping** a PCA residual. The geometry problem is different: MiniRocket PPVs are binomial-like, strongly correlated, and used with Euclidean 3NN in 4096-D with \(n\le 1000\). Distances concentrate; sample covariance is singular; small-eigen directions are where many whole-series class shifts show up; local gap scores also flag sparse but valid normal modes, which is costly at FP0 / 0.1% FPR.

**Spend the MiniRocket-reuse slots on (i) shrinkage that amplifies regularized residual energy instead of discarding it, and (ii) subspace pooling that restores distance contrast.** Put VST in a nested on/off switch, not as its own method. **Do not** spend a candidate on a new 3NN head: LOF already lost, and any strictly monotone map of LocalGap cannot change ROC. **Candidate 3** should be complementary: low-dimensional multiscale discrepancy plus TRAIN-only outlier exposure, fused with a non-OE normal model so the head cannot become only a synthetic detector.

**Monotone reranks (cannot improve ROC / TPR@FPR):** \(f(s)\) strictly increasing in one score; calibration; rank/percentile of one score; changing \(10^{-9}\).  
**Can change ROC:** coordinate VST, whitening, bags, \(k\)/metric/reference, fusion of scores that are not monotone functions of each other.

## TRAIN-only selection (locked)

Synthetics and folds may use **normal TRAIN only**. Never TEST scores or labels.

**Reference set:** same cap as baseline, \(N=\min(n,1000)\), one seeded subsample if \(n>1000\).

**Folds:** 5-fold if \(n\ge 40\); 3-fold if \(15\le n<40\); if \(n<15\), fit on all TRAIN, score normals with leave-one-out for local methods, synthetics against the full reference.

**Four TRAIN-only synthetic types** (each held-out normal → one series per type; then row z-norm):  
1. **Block-shuffle** — 8 contiguous blocks, random permutation.  
2. **Phase-randomize** — real FFT, random phases with conjugate symmetry, iFFT.  
3. **Reverse** — full time reversal.  
4. **Occlusion** — one contiguous block of 15% length set to the series median.

Do **not** use i.i.d. noise, amplitude jitter (destroyed by z-norm), or mixup of normals (stays inside the class hull). Cyclic shifts are a weak negative control only, not a selection type.

**Inner scores (pseudo-test = held-out normals + synthetics):**  
Empirical 0.1% FPR is not identifiable for small folds (often \(<1\) normal). Do not select on inner TPR@0.1%. Use:

- \(t_{d,f}=\min(q_{0.99},\,1-1/n_{\text{hold}})\) quantile of held-out **normal** scores (threshold from normals only).  
- \(\mathrm{Rec}_{d,f,\text{type}}=\) synthetic recall above that threshold.  
- \(J_{d,f}=\min_{\text{type}}\mathrm{Rec}_{d,f,\text{type}}\) (worst-type, not mean-type).  
- \(J_d=\mathrm{mean}_f J_{d,f}\).  
- Secondary tie-break: MAD-normalized gap \(\mathrm{median}(s_{\text{synth}})-\mathrm{median}(s_{\text{hold-n}})\) with a penalty on held-out-normal score SD.

**Family-balanced winner:** \(J_F(c)=\mathrm{mean}_{d\in F} J_d(c)\), \(J(c)=\mathrm{mean}_F J_F(c)\) over 128 families. Winner \(c^\star=\arg\max_c J(c)\). Inside \(c^\star\), per-dataset grid picks are allowed. Freeze before any TEST. Report all three frozen candidates; do not TEST-pick an ensemble. If a TRAIN-only fusion of the three is ever added, weights come from \(J\) only and then freeze.

Per-dataset grids that can collapse to the baseline must include that collapse (so a candidate is allowed to become “baseline-like” when its extra machinery hurts on synthetics).

---

## Experiment 1 — VST + residual-preserving shrinkage whitening (VWRG)

**Question:** Does **regularized inversion** of MiniRocket covariance beat Euclidean LocalGap at low FPR, **without dropping** the residual that 24D/42D routers discarded?

**Pipeline (TRAIN fit only):**  
1. Row z-norm, official aeon MiniRocket 4096 (fixed).  
2. Optional VST **before** the scaler: \(\phi(p)=\arcsin\sqrt{\mathrm{clip}(p,0,1)}\). Nested \(\phi\in\{\text{off},\text{on}\}\).  
3. RobustScaler q10–90, then clip to \([-5,5]\) for covariance only.  
4. Shrinkage covariance on the \(N\times 4096\) reference  
   \[
   S_\lambda=(1-\lambda)S+\lambda\,\tau I,\quad
   S=\mathrm{Cov}(X),\quad
   \tau=\mathrm{mean}\,\mathrm{diag}(S),\quad
   \lambda\in\{0.15,0.35,0.6,0.85\}.
   \]
   Center \(\mu\) = TRAIN mean after the scaler.  
5. Whitened vector \(y=S_\lambda^{-1/2}(x-\mu)\) via eigendecomposition; floor eigenvalues at \(\alpha\,\mathrm{median}(\{\lambda_i>0\})\), \(\alpha=0.1\). **Keep all 4096 whitened coordinates** (tiny eigens are damped, not dropped).  
6. Also store a 1-D residual channel from a **truncated** view used only as an extra coordinate, not as a replacement:
   \[
   r=\|(I-P_k)(x-\mu)\|_2,\quad
   q=r\big/\big(\mathrm{median}_{\mathrm{TRAIN}}(r)+10^{-9}\big),
   \]
   \(k=\min(32,N-2)\), \(P_k\) = top-\(k\) PCA projector on the scaled features. Representation for kNN: \(\tilde y=[y_{\text{(optional subsample of 512 largest-variance whitened coords)}}; q]\). Nested: **full \(y\)** vs **\(y\)+ \(q\)** is unnecessary if using full whitened \(y\); default **score on full \(y\)**.

**Scores (fusion is not a monotone rerank of LocalGap):**  
\[
s_G=\|y\|_2^2,\qquad
s_L=\mathrm{LocalGap}_{3\mathrm{NN}}(y)
\]
with the **same** LocalGap formula as the baseline, radii on TRAIN-only.  
\[
s=\frac{s_G}{\mathrm{median}_{\mathrm{TRAIN}}(s_G)+10^{-9}}
+\beta\frac{s_L}{\mathrm{median}_{\mathrm{TRAIN}}(s_L)+10^{-9}}.
\]
Nested \(\beta\in\{0,0.25,1\}\). **Default \(\beta=0\)** (pure whitened energy). LocalGap is the low-FPR risk; \(\beta=0\) is the intended operating point unless inner \(J_d\) says otherwise. If \(n<20\), force \(\beta=0\).

**Why this is not PCA routing:** dropped-PC routers throw away SPE/Q. Whitening **amplifies** regularized small-eigen directions. That is the opposite failure mode of 24D/42D.

**Failure modes:** \(\lambda\) too small amplifies TRAIN noise → TEST-normal tail FPs; \(\lambda\) too large recovers Euclidean; multimodal normals make \(s_G\) flag valid modes (\(\beta\) should rise only if synthetics are not just “other modes”); VST stretches Bernoulli noise on short series; anomalies that live **inside** the high-variance normal subspace with only density change may need \(\beta>0\).

---

## Experiment 2 — Structured subspace LocalGap (SBLG)

**Question:** Is the loss from LOF / extra Rocket variants about **full-space concentration**, not about MiniRocket features?

**Do not change the feature extractor or VST here** (isolates geometry). Same row z-norm, MiniRocket 4096, RobustScaler q10–90, cap 1000, 3NN LocalGap formula.

**Bags:** \(B=32\). If kernel/dilation IDs are available, split features into those groups and draw bags as **unions of groups** until dimension \(\approx 256\); else uniform sample \(f=256\) features without replacement. Always include **bag 0 = full 4096-D LocalGap** (so the method can revert).

**Pool:**
\[
s=(1-\gamma)\,s_{\mathrm{full}}+\gamma\,\mathrm{Quantile}_\tau\{s_b\}_{b=1}^{B}.
\]
Nested \(\gamma\in\{0,0.5,1\}\), \(\tau\in\{0.5,0.9\}\). Default \(\gamma=0.5\), \(\tau=0.5\).  
\(\tau=0.5\): consensus isolation. \(\tau=0.9\): anomalous in some band (higher FP risk).

**Failure modes:** anomalies that are a **weak coherent shift across all kernels** lose SNR in bags (\(\gamma\to 0\), no gain); \(\tau=0.9\) raises FP0; group bags that ignore dilation structure behave like random subspace LOF (already a losing family in full space). This experiment **must** keep \(\gamma=0\) on the grid or it cannot fail safe.

---

## Experiment 3 — Multiscale discrepancy + constrained outlier exposure (MDOE)

**Question:** Complementary signal: temporal inhomogeneity + a linear synthetic discriminator, **without** concatenating another Rocket explosion (MultiRocket/Hydra already lost).

**3a. Shared-kernel temporal discrepancy (4-D, not \(7\times4096\)):**  
Fit MiniRocket once on the full series. Re-apply the **same** kernels, dilations, and biases to four contiguous quarter-segments. If \(L\) is too short for the largest dilation (gate: skip 3a when a quarter is shorter than the effective support), \(c=0\).

\[
d_j=\sqrt{\frac14\sum_{b=1}^{4}(\mathrm{PPV}_{b,j}-\mathrm{PPV}_{\mathrm{full},j})^2}.
\]
RobustScaler on \(d\) (TRAIN), then
\[
c=\big(\|g\|_2,\; \max_j g_j,\; q_{90}(g),\; q_{50}(g)\big)\in\mathbb{R}^4.
\]
Score \(s_T=\|g\|_2\) (TRAIN-median normalized). This is a **summary**, not a pyramid concatenation.

**3b. Linear OE on MiniRocket + \(c\):**  
Features \(u=[x_{\mathrm{scaled}}; c]\). Labels: TRAIN normals vs the four synthetic types (balance by type). Ridge:
\[
\min_w \;\frac1{n}\|X_+w\|_2^2+\frac1{m}\|X_-w-1\|_2^2+\eta\|w\|_2^2,
\]
normals targeted to 0, synthetics to 1. Nested \(\eta\in\{10^{-1},1,10,10^2\}\). Score \(s_{\mathrm{OE}}=w^\top u\).

**3c. Anchor that cannot overfit synthetics:**  
\(s_N=\|y\|_2^2\) from Experiment 1 with **fixed** \(\lambda=0.35\), VST off (not re-selected on TEST; may share the E1 matrix if E1 is run first, else fit inside E3).

\[
s=\frac{s_N}{\mathrm{median}(s_N)+10^{-9}}
+\delta\frac{s_T}{\mathrm{median}(s_T)+10^{-9}}
+\kappa\frac{s_{\mathrm{OE}}}{\mathrm{median}(s_{\mathrm{OE}})+10^{-9}}.
\]
Nested \(\delta,\kappa\in\{0,0.5,1\}\) with **constraint \(\kappa\le 1\) and \(\delta+\kappa\le 1.5\)**, and **invalidate any grid point whose worst-type inner recall is 0 while another type is \(>0.9\)** (classic OE collapse). Default \(\delta=0.5\), \(\kappa=0.5\). If \(n<20\), \(\kappa=0\).

**Failure modes:** \(w\) becomes a block-shuffle detector; other-class anomalies are coherent shapes and can look **less** synthetic than shuffled normals; seasonality/trend in a valid class inflates \(s_T\); short series disable 3a; OE without the \(\min_{\text{type}}\) rule will win inner mean recall and lose real shifts.

---

## Critical risk checklist

1. **Inner 0.1% FPR is unidentified** on small TRAIN — selecting on it overfits one or two normal scores. Use the quantile/worst-type proxy above.  
2. **Old TEST is contaminated** — even a freeze-then-report on those TEST labels is an upward-biased development number; it is not confirmation of unseen families.  
3. **Monotone cosmetics** — new LocalGap algebra, log-scores, rank calibration: skip.  
4. **PCA drop vs shrink** — repeating 24D/42D without a residual/whitened tail repeats a known loss.  
5. **OE–reality gap** — synthetics destroy order/phase; archive anomalies are often other classes. Worst-type \(J\) and the \(s_N\) anchor are mandatory, not optional.  
6. **Family imbalance** — micro-average over 1117 datasets will select for large families. Use \(\mathrm{mean}_F\).  
7. **Multimodal normals** — global \(s_G\) raises FP0; that is why \(\beta\) is nested, default 0 only as a low-FPR prior.  
8. **Short series / pyramid gate** — do not silently run quarter-PPV with broken dilations.  
9. **Cap-1000 subsample leak** — same subset for scaler, covariance, kNN, and OE; do not refit on a different draw after seeing inner scores.  
10. **Post-hoc TEST fusion of E1–E3** — forbidden. A three-way blend is a fourth method and needs its own TRAIN-only freeze.  
11. **Claiming the 10% relative lift before a frozen run** — not supported. E1 has the strongest prior (correlation + residual). E2 is the cheapest falsification of concentration. E3 is the only bet on unseen **shape** shifts and the most likely to overfit synthetics.  
12. **Implementation parity** — row z-norm, aeon MiniRocket 4096, cap 1000, RobustScaler q10–90, LocalGap formula, and family-mean TPR at FP0 / 0.1% / 0.5% / 1% must match the baseline exactly when extra knobs are off (\(\phi\) off, \(\beta=0\) with \(\lambda\to 1\), or \(\gamma=0\), or \(\delta=\kappa=0\)).

**Codex:** implement E1–E3 as three independent scorers with the grids above, the shared synthetic/fold harness, family-balanced \(J\), and a single freeze artifact (winner + per-dataset params). No TEST in that loop. After freeze, report family-mean TPR at FP0, 0.1%, 0.5%, 1% for all three plus baseline.
